record_identity.title: German television personality alleged deepfake pornography was distributed using her likeness

incident_identity.date_basis: The public record establishes the occurrence through later reporting and complaint-related coverage but does not expose a single independently verified generation timestamp.

summary: Sexual deepfake imagery using German television personality Collien Fernandes’ likeness circulated and prompted her complaint, threats, police protection, public demonstrations and debate over German law. Fernandes alleged her former husband Christian Ulmen distributed material; he denied responsibility. In May 2026 a Hamburg court, deciding an interim press-law application against Der Spiegel, found sufficient evidential basis to report the suspicion that he distributed others’ deepfake videos, but said the article did not imply he made them. The ruling did not determine criminal responsibility. The generating service, source-to-output chain and ultimate authorship remain unestablished in this Case File.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Reuters, the Guardian and El País report sexual deepfake imagery using Fernandes’ likeness, her complaint and serious public consequences while preserving Ulmen’s denial. The Hamburg Regional Court press release states that its interim ruling allowed reporting a suspicion of distribution because a minimum evidential basis existed, but the article did not imply Ulmen generated videos made by others; the ruling did not decide criminal responsibility. The available sources do not identify the generating system or disclose its request, consent-control state or source-to-output records. The identity-bound sexual portrayal and complaint are supported; the system-side authority mechanism and named actor attribution remain unresolved.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence has two separable components: an identity-bound sexual portrayal whose production/requester authority pathway is not shown, and a disputed distribution allegation subject to a limited interim press-law threshold. The current record supports neither a finding that the requester or generator treated access to the likeness as permission nor a finding about who generated the files. Identity-Representation Authority Separation therefore remains unresolved at clause level; the court’s reporting threshold does not resolve the technical or criminal attribution question. The unresolved identity-authority question is bounded by missing production and requester/consent evidence, not by a requirement to identify a generator alone. A requester-side mechanism could satisfy the neutral class, but the court’s distribution-reporting threshold does not reconstruct that mechanism or establish criminal responsibility. No reviewed local requirement candidate or independent admitted canonical duty is established.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This case calls for preserving distinct states for an evidenced sexual identity-bound output, unknown generator-side consent handling, disputed distribution attribution, and an interim court’s limited assessment of reportability. Publicly unavailable forensic material does not by itself establish that a synthesis system failed to retain provenance. The clause analysis leaves the authority-control question unresolved pending evidence of the generating pathway.
assessment_boundaries: Ulmen denied responsibility; VIGIL does not adjudicate who created or distributed the images.
The generating model, service and provider-side request or consent-control state are not identified in the available evidence.

The identity-representation authority class remains unresolved because necessary generator-side recognition facts are unavailable; the record does not infer that absence of public evidence proves absence of consent or controls.
The Hamburg Regional Court interim press-law ruling assessed permissible suspicion reporting and did not determine criminal liability or technical authorship.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Separate the evidenced identity-bound sexual representation from the disputed attribution and the limited evidentiary threshold established in the interim press-law ruling.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Sexual deepfake imagery using Collien Fernandes’ likeness was reported and became the subject of her complaint; the available reporting does not identify the generating service or disclose its request and consent-control state.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: For a materially consent-sensitive identity-bound synthesis, a valid authority basis must be established before generation; a public report of the output alone does not show whether or how the generator tested that basis.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The identity-bound sexual portrayal materially engages the neutral authority invariant, which can be evidenced at requester or generator level. Here the sources do not reconstruct the source-to-output/requester pathway or its consent/other authority basis; the distribution allegation cannot supply those production facts. Neither failure nor success is established.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Fernandes alleged her former husband distributed the deepfake videos and he denied it. In an interim press-law ruling, the court found sufficient basis to report suspicion of distribution of videos made by others, while saying the article did not imply that he created them.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A disputed allegation of distribution, a reportable suspicion under interim press-law review, and proof of who generated the material are distinct evidentiary states and should not be collapsed.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The Hamburg court found sufficient evidential basis to report a suspicion of distribution of others’ deepfake videos, but did not read the article as alleging their creation by Ulmen.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Distribution attribution and generation attribution must remain separate; a press-law evidential threshold is not a forensic source-to-output chain or criminal verdict.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The court’s interim finding concerns reportable suspicion of distribution of others’ videos, not the production/requester pathway or separately established identity-use authority. Requester-side evidence could satisfy the class without identifying a generator, but it is not established by this distribution threshold.

The public record does not reconstruct the source-to-output lineage, but absence of that lineage from VIGIL's sources does not establish that a governed synthesis process itself failed to preserve required antecedent traceability. Reviewer evidence limits are not an occurrence-level Synthesis Traceability failure.
